data.body:
Implementation pushed for review as Gerrit change 1650 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1650), commit 94a537e2aa.

SHAPE CHOSEN: distinct journal patterns into distinct METRIC NAMES, not a CloudWatch dimension. observability.sh §4e reuses the existing publish_autodeploy_marker_delta helper (whose first argument is already an ERE handed to grep -cE) with two new offset files, emitting review_interrupts_bound_exceeded and review_interrupts_signal_unavailable alongside the UNCHANGED rolled-up review_interrupts. Everything stays dimensionless on both sides, so the monitoring_s4b.tf silent-unmatch hazard cannot bite (AC3 holds trivially). monitoring_autodeploy.tf replaces the single alarm with one alarm per reason, each carrying only its own remediation; the rolled-up metric is still published but no longer alarmed, so an interrupt never double-pages.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: re-tuning bound-exceeded's sensitivity. Both alarms keep the pre-split 900s / 1-datapoint / Sum > 0 / notBreaching cadence, so the split changes no sensitivity and signal-unavailable still latches on one datapoint (AC2). Making bound-exceeded quieter belongs with the DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX disposition, not here.

COORDINATION: kept disjoint from bug 2dc7 (affluent-conveyable-dromedary, Gerrit 1648), which rewrites the negative-delta clamp INSIDE the helpers. My edits are the comment block, the offset-file declarations and the call sites; the helper's offset/clamp logic is untouched. Verified against 1648's current diff — no overlapping lines.

VERIFICATION (no host shell access needed for any of it): new tests/scripts/test_observability_interrupt_reasons.py drives the REAL observability.sh over a synthetic unit journal, including the piranha case itself — four firings that are ALL bound-exceeded leave review_interrupts_signal_unavailable at 0, which is exactly the discrimination 7b4a needed SSM for. 28 passed across the new file plus test_observability_offsets_6a65.py, test_observability_exit.py and test_autodeploy_review_drain.py. terraform fmt -check and terraform validate both clean — validate caught a real constraint on the way, CloudWatch caps alarm_description at 1024 chars, and both descriptions were tightened under it; CI's terraform-drift workflow runs the same two checks.

STILL OPEN: AC4. This is a Terraform alarm-contract change and takes effect only on an operator terraform apply, not on merge.
